output_scripts.code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Configuration (use workspace from container context)
WORKDIR="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/employee-management-portal-66484-66615/FrontendApplication"
PROFILE="/etc/profile.d/frontend_app_env.sh"
# Defaults
NODE_ENV_DEFAULT="development"
PORT_DEFAULT="3000"

# Ensure workspace exists and is owned by current user
sudo mkdir -p "$WORKDIR" && sudo chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" "$WORKDIR"

# Validate node exists and major >= 18
NODE_V_RAW=$(command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 && node -v || true)
if [[ -z "$NODE_V_RAW" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: node not found on PATH" >&2
  exit 2
fi
NODE_MAJOR=$(echo "$NODE_V_RAW" | sed -E 's/^v?([0-9]+).*$/\1/')
if ! [[ "$NODE_MAJOR" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: unable to parse node version: $NODE_V_RAW" >&2
  exit 3
fi
if (( NODE_MAJOR < 18 )); then
  echo "ERROR: node major version $NODE_MAJOR < 18 required" >&2
  exit 4
fi

# Validate npm exists
if ! command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: npm not found on PATH" >&2
  exit 5
fi

# Compute npm global bin in a robust way
NPM_GLOBAL_BIN=$(npm bin -g 2>/dev/null || true)
# Fallback common locations if npm didn't provide
if [[ -z "$NPM_GLOBAL_BIN" ]]; then
  if [[ -d "$HOME/.npm-global/bin" ]]; then
    NPM_GLOBAL_BIN="$HOME/.npm-global/bin"
  else
    # fallback to /usr/local/bin (common global bin)
    NPM_GLOBAL_BIN="/usr/local/bin"
  fi
fi

# Build idempotent profile fragment content
# We'll export NODE_ENV and PORT only if not already set to desired values, and prepend npm global bin to PATH if missing
TMPFILE=$(mktemp)
cat > "$TMPFILE" <<'EOF'
# frontend_app environment variables - managed by env-01-setup
# Preserve existing PATH and prepend npm global bin if not present
export NODE_ENV="__NODE_ENV__"
export PORT="__PORT__"
# Prepend NPM_GLOBAL_BIN to PATH if not already present
if [[ -d "__NPM_GLOBAL_BIN__" ]] && ! echo ":$PATH:" | grep -q ":__NPM_GLOBAL_BIN__:"; then
  export PATH="__NPM_GLOBAL_BIN__:$PATH"
fi
EOF

# Replace placeholders safely
sed -i "s|__NODE_ENV__|${NODE_ENV_DEFAULT}|g" "$TMPFILE"
sed -i "s|__PORT__|${PORT_DEFAULT}|g" "$TMPFILE"
sed -i "s|__NPM_GLOBAL_BIN__|${NPM_GLOBAL_BIN}|g" "$TMPFILE"

# Ensure profile file exists and is idempotent: we will create/replace a block between markers
START_MARKER="# >>> frontend_app env (managed) >>>"
END_MARKER="# <<< frontend_app env (managed) <<<"
NEW_BLOCK="$START_MARKER\n$(cat "$TMPFILE")\n$END_MARKER"
rm -f "$TMPFILE"

# Write atomically to a temp file then install with sudo
OUT_TMP=$(mktemp)
echo -e "$NEW_BLOCK" > "$OUT_TMP"
# If profile exists, remove existing managed block then append
if sudo test -f "$PROFILE"; then
  # remove existing managed block if present
  sudo awk -v s="$START_MARKER" -v e="$END_MARKER" '
  BEGIN{p=1}
  {
    if($0==s) {p=0}
    if(p) print $0
    if($0==e) {p=1}
  }' "$PROFILE" > "$PROFILE.tmp.clean" || true
  # append new block
  sudo bash -c "cat '$PROFILE.tmp.clean' > '$PROFILE' && printf '\n' >> '$PROFILE' && cat '$OUT_TMP' >> '$PROFILE'"
  sudo rm -f "$PROFILE.tmp.clean"
else
  sudo bash -c "cat '$OUT_TMP' > '$PROFILE'"
fi
rm -f "$OUT_TMP"

# Ensure profile file is readable
sudo chmod 644 "$PROFILE"

# Source the profile in current shell (use bash -c to get same expansions)
# Use dot-sourcing in this shell to validate exports
# Note: /etc/profile.d scripts are written for sh-compatible shells; source with bash
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
. "$PROFILE"

# Validate exports are present
if [[ "${NODE_ENV:-}" != "$NODE_ENV_DEFAULT" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: NODE_ENV not exported as $NODE_ENV_DEFAULT (got: ${NODE_ENV:-})" >&2
  exit 6
fi
if [[ "${PORT:-}" != "$PORT_DEFAULT" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: PORT not exported as $PORT_DEFAULT (got: ${PORT:-})" >&2
  exit 7
fi
# Validate npm global bin in PATH (use computed value)
if [[ -d "$NPM_GLOBAL_BIN" ]]; then
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$NPM_GLOBAL_BIN:") ;;
    *) echo "ERROR: npm global bin $NPM_GLOBAL_BIN not present in PATH after sourcing" >&2; exit 8 ;;
  esac
fi

# Final success output minimal
echo "OK: environment persisted to $PROFILE, NODE_ENV=$NODE_ENV, PORT=$PORT, npm_global_bin=$NPM_GLOBAL_BIN"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKDIR="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/employee-management-portal-66484-66615/FrontendApplication"
cd "$WORKDIR"
. /etc/profile.d/frontend_app_env.sh

setsid ./node_modules/.bin/webpack serve --mode development --host 0.0.0.0 --port "$PORT" > "$WORKDIR/logs/dev_server.log" 2>&1 &
# give a moment then find process listening on port

# find the process (prefer matching webpack-dev-server / webpack serve)
SERVER_PID=$(pgrep -f "webpack.*serve" | head -n1 || true)

steps.name: Validation: build, serve production bundle, smoke HTTP and tests, and cleanup
steps.description: Validate environment by building production bundle (build-01), serving the dist directory via a small static server (prefer npx http-server or Python http.server fallback), poll HTTP until reachable, run tests, and cleanly stop the static server. This avoids mixing production build with dev-server. Provide evidence (HTTP status and snippet) and ensure cleanup of PID and logs.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKDIR="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/employee-management-portal-66484-66615/FrontendApplication"
cd "$WORKDIR"
. /etc/profile.d/frontend_app_env.sh
PORT=${PORT:-3000}
# ensure build exists
./node_modules/.bin/webpack --mode production --config webpack.config.js || { echo 'ERROR: webpack build failed' >&2; exit 18; }
if [[ ! -d dist ]]; then echo 'ERROR: dist missing after build' >&2; exit 19; fi
# start a simple static server to serve dist
mkdir -p logs
# prefer npx http-server if available in node_modules or globally, else python fallback
if [[ -x ./node_modules/.bin/http-server ]]; then SERV_BIN="./node_modules/.bin/http-server"; SERV_ARGS=(dist -p "$PORT"); elif command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then SERV_BIN="npx"; SERV_ARGS=(http-server dist -p "$PORT" --silent); else # python fallback
  SERV_BIN="python3"; SERV_ARGS=( -m http.server "$PORT" --directory dist ); fi
# start server in background and capture PID
setsid $SERV_BIN "${SERV_ARGS[@]}" > "$WORKDIR/logs/validation_server.log" 2>&1 &
sleep 1
VALID_PID=$(pgrep -f "http.server\|http-server" | head -n1 || true)
if [[ -z "$VALID_PID" ]]; then echo 'ERROR: static server failed to start; see logs' >&2; tail -n 200 "$WORKDIR/logs/validation_server.log" || true; exit 20; fi
echo "$VALID_PID" > "$WORKDIR/.validation_server.pid"
trap 'kill ${VALID_PID:-0} 2>/dev/null || true; rm -f "$WORKDIR/.validation_server.pid"' EXIT
# poll
URL="http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/"
TIMEOUT=60
SECONDS=0
while true; do
  if status=$(curl -fsS -o /tmp/validate_response.txt -w "%{http_code}" "$URL" || true); then
    if [[ "$status" == "200" ]]; then
      echo "HTTP 200 from $URL"
      head -c 200 /tmp/validate_response.txt | sed -n '1,5p'
      break
    fi
  fi
  if (( SECONDS >= TIMEOUT )); then echo "ERROR: timeout polling $URL" >&2; exit 21; fi
  sleep 1
done
# run tests to ensure test pipeline still passes
./node_modules/.bin/jest --colors --runInBand || { echo 'ERROR: tests failed during validation' >&2; exit 22; }
# cleanup (trap will kill)
kill "$VALID_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f "$WORKDIR/.validation_server.pid"
exit 0

This plan preserves existing step structure but modifies scripts to address critical and high recommendations (safe PATH handling, robust Node version check, proper install commands, avoiding injection of $PORT into package.json, safer backgrounding and PID handling, validation approach, and removing '|| true' that masks failures).

change_logs.message: Refined plan to address analyst feedback: Fixed env-01 to write a valid /etc/profile.d/frontend_app_env.sh and validated it; replaced jq usage in scaffold-01 with a node-based package.json edit and added idempotency for file writes; updated deps-01 (renamed script_name to 'install') to pin React to ^18.2.0 and to add babel-jest and jest pinned versions; adjusted test-01 to use npm run test (local jest) and ensured jest config references babel-jest; hardened validation-01 to correctly set PORT, increase poll timeout, use curl -fsS for checks, assert HTTP 200 and expected content, add trap to cleanup the dev server, and ensure profile is sourced so env vars are visible. These changes address CRITICAL and HIGH items (env file correctness, jq removal, babel-jest addition, test execution method, validation robustness) and several MEDIUM/LOW recommendations (version pinning, idempotency, cleanup).

Refined plan to address analyst feedback: completed and corrected env-01 script (safe, idempotent /etc/profile.d write, compute npm global bin, source for current shell, validate node>=18 and npm); added scaffold-01 to create a minimal React app (idempotent, plain JS, webpack+babel config); added deps-01 to install exact dependencies/devDependencies into the workspace using npm and verify local node_modules; added test-01 to configure babel-jest, create a lightweight smoke test and run npm test via local jest; added build-01 to run production build and verify artifacts; added start-01 to run the dev server bound to 0.0.0.0 in background and capture PID; added validate-01 to build, start, poll endpoint with curl -fsS, assert HTTP 200 and expected content, run tests, and cleanly stop server. These changes address CRITICAL and HIGH analyst items (complete scripts for environment, scaffolding, install, test, build, start, validation), implement idempotency and version validation, and ensure headless, non-interactive operation.

Refined steps env-01, scaffold-01, deps-01, test-01, build-01, start-01 and validate-01 to address analyst feedback: (1) env-01: replaced brittle regex with numeric Node major check, compute npm global bin safely, append (not overwrite) PATH in /etc/profile.d, validate exports after sourcing and fail fast; (2) scaffold-01: avoid injecting $PORT, set start script to use process.env.PORT fallback, add 'private': true and 'main' fields, add .gitignore, and ensure webpack config reads process.env.PORT; (3) deps-01: remove 'npm ci || true', use 'npm install --no-audit --no-fund --silent' when deps missing, pin html-webpack-plugin and babel packages, validate node_modules contents after install; (4) test-01: merge jest config non-destructively, verify babel-jest installed and jest binary exists, run tests without hiding failures; (5) start-01: run local binary (./node_modules/.bin/webpack serve) via setsid to capture the actual server PID and write logs to workspace/logs; (6) build-01 and validate-01: clarify validation flow — validation builds production bundle and serves it via a lightweight static server (using npx http-server if available or a small Python http.server fallback) to validate artifacts; dev-server start is a separate step which captures the server PID robustly. Also reduced uses of '|| true', added lightweight validations after key operations, and moved logs to workspace for persistence. These changes address CRITICAL/HIGH items about version checks, install reliability, env persistence, PID handling, and package.json safety.
